title: Between Atlas and Sea
subject: morocco
author: Clueberry Desk
introduction: Ten Moroccan towns, ordered by nothing except the way the letters fit.

entries.clue: Rif town whose lanes are washed in blue
Desert-edge town with film studios on its outskirts
Windy Atlantic port inside eighteenth-century ramparts
Port looking across the strait at Spain
Northern city carrying a strong Andalusi imprint
Imperial city of Moulay Ismail's granaries and stables
Southern beach city rebuilt after the 1960 earthquake
Walled old quarter, whatever the town
Administrative capital at the mouth of the Bouregreg
City of the Qarawiyyin, and a brimless hat

factCards.text: The medina of Tetouan was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1997, cited for its Andalusi architecture.
factCards.sourceTitle: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Medina of Tetouan

factCards.text: Agadir was largely destroyed by an earthquake on 29 February 1960 and rebuilt on a new site to the south.
factCards.sourceTitle: USGS Earthquake Hazards Program — Significant earthquakes archive, Agadir 1960

factCards.text: Essaouira's fortified town was laid out from the 1760s to a plan drawing on European military engineering; the extent of any single designer's role is debated by historians.
factCards.sourceTitle: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Medina of Essaouira (formerly Mogador)
